gate1.note: User selected Feature + Autopilot at the front door after being shown the measured root cause. A production BFF session survives exactly one refresh: the Hub rotates its session cookie as __Host-fxl_hub_session in production, and hub-sdk 1.3.1's parseRotatedRefresh regex cannot match a name preceded by '-', so tx.update is never called and the store replays a stale refresh token until the Hub revokes the family with reuse_detected. Invisible locally because the Hub only prefixes the cookie when NODE_ENV=production, which is why three prior browser-side fixes all missed it. Four independent slices in one wave: slice 01 normalizes the rotated cookie name at createHubBff's fetchImpl seam and adds the end-to-end oracle that was missing; slices 02-04 repair the /no-role dead end that earlier fixes turned a lost session into. Gate 2 remains mandatory per slice and per wave. Gate 3 remains human-gated; this run stops at master.
gate1.outcome: All four slices merged to master and each passed Gate 2 by a separate Verify agent, plus a wave-verify on integrated master (1203 tests, lint, type-check, real build, security review). Root cause was upstream of this repo: hub-sdk 1.3.1's parseRotatedRefresh cannot match the __Host-fxl_hub_session name the Hub uses in production. Fixed here at createHubBff's fetchImpl seam; the real one-line SDK fix is filed in nexo/ROADMAP.md for 16--INTERNAL--fxl-hub. Wave ran serially because nexo-wave-exec.sh hardcodes the 'main' trunk and pnpm worktrees lack node_modules; Gate 2 was not weakened. Mutation tooling is not configured, so per-slice mutation proofs stood in. Not promoted: this run stops at master pending the operator's own check.

gate1_prior.note: User selected Autopilot at the front door, and pre-answered the one design fork that mattered: keep our own session store, do not adopt SqlHubSessionStore.
